questions.prompt: Qual problema este projeto precisa resolver?
Quem usará ou será afetado pelo resultado?
Como reconheceremos que o projeto teve sucesso?
O que precisa fazer parte da primeira entrega?
O que explicitamente não faz parte desta entrega?
Que classificação possuem os dados envolvidos?
Quais ações o agente pode executar sem nova aprovação?

drivers.prompt: How complex and changeable are the business rules?
How many external systems or infrastructure providers must be isolated?
Is delivery organized mainly by end-to-end features or shared technical layers?
How strongly must business behavior be testable without UI, database or network?

options.name: Pragmatic layered architecture
options.summary: Separates presentation, application and data concerns with a deliberately small abstraction budget.

options.name: Ports and adapters
options.summary: Keeps application and domain behavior behind explicit ports implemented by replaceable adapters.

options.name: Clean Architecture
options.summary: Organizes dependencies inward around entities and use cases, independent of delivery and infrastructure details.

options.name: Vertical Slice Architecture
options.summary: Groups code and behavior by use case so each feature can evolve with minimal cross-feature coupling.

drivers.prompt: Do changes usually stay inside one feature or cross many features in the same technical layer?
Is ownership assigned by product capability or technical specialty?
What is the expected project size and lifetime?

options.name: Layer-first organization
options.summary: Groups files by technical role such as UI, services, domain and data.

options.name: Feature-first organization
options.summary: Co-locates a feature's UI, behavior, tests and infrastructure-facing code behind an explicit feature boundary.

options.name: Hybrid feature-first with internal layers
options.summary: Uses features as top-level boundaries and lightweight technical layers only inside features that need them.

drivers.prompt: Do capabilities require independent deployment and scaling?
Can the team operate distributed systems reliably?
Are stable bounded contexts already known?
Does the core workflow require simple transactional consistency?

options.name: Monolith
options.summary: Delivers the application as one deployable unit with minimal internal module enforcement.

options.name: Modular monolith
options.summary: Uses enforced domain modules inside one deployable unit, preserving an extraction path if independence becomes necessary.

options.name: Microservices
options.summary: Deploys bounded capabilities independently and treats network, data ownership and operations as first-class constraints.

rankings.name: Ports and adapters
reasons: +4 domain:complex: Strong boundaries isolate complex business behavior.
tradeoffs: More interfaces, mapping and initial design effort

rankings.name: Clean Architecture
reasons: +4 domain:complex: Use-case and domain boundaries protect complex business policy.
+2 integrations:many: Outer layers isolate volatile frameworks and services.
tradeoffs: Explicit dependency direction and long-lived domain isolation
More concepts and mapping code to maintain consistently

rankings.name: Vertical Slice Architecture
tradeoffs: Localized feature changes and reduced cross-feature coupling
Shared behavior needs deliberate extraction to avoid duplication

rankings.name: Pragmatic layered architecture
reasons: -3 domain:complex: Complex business rules need stronger dependency isolation.
tradeoffs: Lower initial ceremony and faster onboarding
Technical layers can become coupled as domain complexity grows

unansweredDrivers.prompt: Is delivery organized mainly by end-to-end features or shared technical layers?
How strongly must business behavior be testable without UI, database or network?

output.name: Meaningful names
output.statement: Names communicate intent using the vocabulary of the problem and remain consistent inside their bounded context.
reviewQuestions: Can a maintainer understand the role without tracing the full implementation?
Do names distinguish business concepts instead of hiding them behind generic labels?
misuseRisks: Renaming without improving shared understanding creates churn and invalidates useful history.
exceptions: Protocol, framework and generated names may be fixed by an external contract.

output.name: Small cohesive units
output.statement: Functions and modules should express one coherent level of intent, with size following responsibility rather than an arbitrary line limit.
reviewQuestions: Does this unit mix policy, orchestration and low-level mechanics without a reason?
Can its behavior be described with one coherent purpose?
misuseRisks: Splitting code solely to reduce line count increases indirection and scatters behavior.
exceptions: A linear algorithm or declarative configuration may be clearer when kept together.

output.name: Explicit error behavior
output.statement: Errors preserve actionable context, distinguish expected failure from defects and never disappear silently.
reviewQuestions: Can callers distinguish retryable, user-correctable and programmer failures?
Does the error retain the relevant cause without exposing sensitive data?
misuseRisks: Excessive custom error types add ceremony without improving recovery decisions.
exceptions: Best-effort telemetry may drop failures when that behavior is explicit and observable.

output.name: Comments explain why
output.statement: Comments record intent, constraints and non-obvious trade-offs instead of narrating code that can explain itself.
reviewQuestions: Does each comment add context the implementation cannot express safely?
Will the comment remain synchronized with the source of truth?
misuseRisks: Deleting every comment removes essential rationale and safety constraints.
exceptions: Public API documentation and legally required notices serve contracts beyond local readability.

output.name: Readable behavioral tests
output.statement: Tests communicate observable behavior, use independent expectations and fail for a specific meaningful regression.
reviewQuestions: Does the test name the production break it catches?
Are expected values independent from the implementation under test?
misuseRisks: Maximizing coverage or mirroring implementation creates brittle tests without confidence.
exceptions: Generated compatibility matrices may favor systematic data over narrative test bodies.

output.name: Visible side effects
output.statement: State mutation, I/O and external effects are explicit at boundaries and separated from deterministic decisions where practical.
reviewQuestions: Can a caller identify which operation changes external or shared state?
Is deterministic policy testable without performing the effect?
misuseRisks: Wrapping every trivial operation behind an interface creates indirection without isolation value.
exceptions: Framework lifecycle methods may define effects implicitly as part of their documented contract.

output.name: Single Responsibility Principle
output.statement: A module should serve one coherent actor or reason for change, not merely contain one method.
reviewQuestions: Are unrelated actors or policies forcing changes in this module?
Does the proposed split follow change responsibility rather than file size?
misuseRisks: Splitting by method count or vague responsibilities creates fragmentation and navigation cost.
exceptions: A small cohesive module may support several operations for the same actor and policy.

output.name: Open-Closed Principle
output.statement: Stable policy should support known extension pressure without repeated invasive modification.
reviewQuestions: Is there demonstrated recurring variation rather than a hypothetical future need?
Does the extension point protect stable policy without hiding simple code?
misuseRisks: Designing speculative extension points creates abstraction debt and unused flexibility.
exceptions: Direct modification is preferable while requirements and boundaries remain uncertain.

output.name: Liskov Substitution Principle
output.statement: Subtypes and implementations preserve the behavioral promises expected through their base contract.
reviewQuestions: Can every implementation be substituted without strengthening preconditions or weakening guarantees?
Are error and side-effect semantics consistent across implementations?
misuseRisks: Applying substitution language to unrelated data shapes can obscure simpler contract defects.
exceptions: Marker types with no behavioral contract require only their explicitly documented semantics.

output.name: Interface Segregation Principle
output.statement: Consumers depend only on the capabilities they use, with interfaces shaped around real client needs.
reviewQuestions: Are clients forced to implement or import operations they do not use?
Would a narrower capability boundary improve ownership and testing?
misuseRisks: One-method interfaces created mechanically can multiply concepts without reducing coupling.
exceptions: Stable external protocols may require a broad interface that local code cannot change.

output.name: Dependency Inversion Principle
output.statement: High-level policy should not depend directly on volatile infrastructure details; both meet at a boundary owned by policy needs.
reviewQuestions: Does volatile infrastructure control the shape of business policy?
Is the abstraction owned by the consumer and justified by volatility or testing needs?
misuseRisks: Abstracting every concrete dependency adds indirection without protecting meaningful policy.
exceptions: Stable language or standard-library primitives can remain direct dependencies.

output.name: KISS and essential simplicity
output.statement: Prefer the simplest design that satisfies current constraints, evidence and required quality attributes.
reviewQuestions: Which complexity is essential to the problem and which was introduced by the solution?
Is there a smaller design with equal correctness, safety and operability?
misuseRisks: Calling a design simple can conceal missing security, reliability or domain requirements.
exceptions: Necessary complexity remains necessary and should be isolated rather than denied.

output.name: YAGNI and evidence-backed scope
output.statement: Do not build speculative capability before a confirmed requirement or a low-cost irreversible constraint justifies it.
reviewQuestions: Which accepted requirement or measured risk requires this capability now?
Can the decision be deferred without closing a critical option?
misuseRisks: YAGNI used blindly can ignore cheap foundations needed for security, migration or irreversible contracts.
exceptions: Security boundaries, data migration paths and public contracts may require early design.

output.name: DRY after knowledge stabilizes
output.statement: Consolidate duplicated knowledge when occurrences share meaning and are expected to change together.
reviewQuestions: Does the duplication represent the same knowledge or only similar syntax?
Have the occurrences demonstrated coordinated change?
misuseRisks: Premature abstraction couples unrelated behavior and turns coincidental similarity into a shared dependency.
exceptions: Independent bounded contexts may intentionally duplicate representations to preserve autonomy.

output.name: Separation of concerns
output.statement: Separate concerns that change, scale, fail or require authority for different reasons while keeping cohesive behavior together.
reviewQuestions: Do these concerns have different change drivers, failure modes or owners?
Does separation reduce coupling more than it increases coordination cost?
misuseRisks: Separating every technical activity can scatter one feature across unnecessary layers.
exceptions: A small cohesive feature may keep presentation and behavior close when boundaries remain explicit.

output.name: Composition over inheritance
output.statement: Prefer explicit composition for varying behavior unless inheritance models a stable substitutable relationship.
reviewQuestions: Is the relationship truly substitutable or only code reuse?
Would composition make dependencies and variation clearer?
misuseRisks: Replacing a small stable hierarchy with excessive delegation can reduce clarity.
exceptions: Framework extension points and proven taxonomies may require inheritance.
